system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period

- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===

# Review: Seller Positions vs. Wattlebridge Playbook — Project Kestrel

## Material Departures Identified

### 1. General warranty cap: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 (not 25% / AUD 6,000,000)
The Seller's starting position, even if negotiable, has dropped below our pre-agreed starting position of 25% / AUD 6,000,000. More critically, the 20% position requires prior written authority from our principal Amelia Frost identifying the draft; none has been given. This cuts buyer warranty exposure by AUD 1,200,000 from our baseline, without any delegation. **Push back immediately.**

### 2. Thresholds: de minimis AUD 25,000; basket AUD 250,000
Our baseline is de minimis AUD 5,000 and aggregate basket AUD 50,000, seller liable from the first dollar once exceeded. The Seller's de minimis of AUD 25,000 raises the bar to trigger recoverability (but still lowers it compared to typical market), while the AUD 250,000 basket dramatically narrows excess recovery. After de minimis is met, the seller recovers essentially nothing above AUD 250,000 — compared to our AUD 50,000. This materially compresses the seller's exposure in any claim rising above those figures. **Push back.**

### 3. Time limits: 18 months general; applied to all claims unless expressly stated otherwise
Our standard general claims period is 24 months after Completion. An 18-month fallback requires Amelia Frost written approval (none given). Further, applying the limitation to "all Claims of any nature" collapses the fundamental/title regime into the general one — directly conflicting with our rule that Title/Tax/IP/payment/covenant categories stay separate and fundamental/title operates under an independent 100% cap at least six years. **Reject the conflation.**

### 4. Limitations & reliance clauses apply to all Claims of any nature
Again combined with items 2–3, this effectively eliminates the separation between general and fundamental/title regimes. Under our playbook, fundamental/title survives its own treatment outside the general basket, de minimis, knowledge bar and time limits. **Push back hard — this is a regime override.**

### 5. Disclosure: Schedule 7 relies on general data-room and public-register disclosure
Our playbook explicitly requires specific fair disclosure and rejects whole-data-room, public-register or prudent-search deemed disclosure. The Seller's "relies on general disclosure" approach would circumvent our due diligence protections entirely. **Force rejection — this is the single biggest procedural departure.**

### 6. Buyer knowledge clause (8.3): blanket exclusion including anything discoverable from the data room or public records
Our rule is to delete blanket exclusions; any qualifier needs named seller knowledge persons plus reasonable enquiry; never excuse title, capacity, fraud or a specific indemnity. Including the data room as "known" defeats meaningful buyer diligence. **Reject.**

### 7. Bluefen consent: reasonable endeavours, satisfied on delivery
Our rule requires effective consent AND evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient for a material customer consent (DD-002 ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue, ~30%, material). The Seller offers nothing delivered at Completion. **Must insist on actual consent plus condition evidence, completed before Closing.**

### 8. Riverlark: release following Completion
Our rule demands current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds AND effective security releases; a post-completion release additionally needs an irrevocable undertaking plus Amelia Frost approval. No undertaking or approval present. **Push back — require undertaking pre-Completion with authority; repaid from Completion funds.**

### 9. DD-005 AUD 420,000 employee bonuses missing from funds flow
Our rule requires DD-005 to be a specific line item or seller-funded, and the funds flow must not silently exclude it. AUD 420,000 in conditional completion bonuses not itemised is a funds-flow anomaly, potentially leaving the seller exposed on accrued amounts and payroll tax/super on-costs. **Push back — require specific line item, seller-funded or included.**

### 10. Ironquay IP: limited to SOW3 payment; considered adequate; AUD 180,000 not independently verified
Our rule is to broaden the narrow indemnity while preserving the SOW3 cure, leaving the AUD 180,000 amount open since neither party has independent bank verification. The Seller wants to close it. **Reject the closure — preserve the broader indemnity.**

### 11. Export/privacy incident (DD-006): preliminary, expected non-material; no investigation demanded
Our rule requires preservation of logs, investigation, updates, and assumes no confirmed breach, harm, notification duty or numeric demand. The Seller discloses only a download link to an unintended external email with ~1,240 records but provides no breach characterization, scope, harm or demand analysis. **Insist on full log preservation, investigation, ongoing updates, and retain open assumption pending conclusion.**

### 12. Supplier renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate): classed as ordinary-course operating costs
Our rule is to assess; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. The Seller is proactively excluding them from price adjustment risk. Without assessment, we lose the ability to verify ordinary course, unavoidable, terminable, accrued status and any pricing impacts. **Push back — require seller-funded assessment; do not classify automatically.**

### 13. Tax / IP: settled under general regime
Our rule keeps tax and IP terms OPEN, assuming no unlimited liability and no resolution. The Seller closed both regimes under the general warranty framework. **Reject the closure — hold both open.**

### 14. Title: DD-012 share register as sole evidence
Our rule requires independent title/ownership/encumbrance/authority evidence; DD-012 is a supplied internal register, not independent proof. The seller relies solely on its own register record with no independent verification. **Push back — require independent title evidence beyond the register.**

---

## Summary Recommendations

| # | Issue | Action |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | Cap 20% vs 25%; no Amelia authority | Revert to 25%/AUD 6M or obtain written authority |
| 2 | Thresholds raised (de minimis & basket) | Restore de minimis AUD 5k, basket AUD 50k; seller liable from first dollar |
| 3 | 18-month time limit; applied to all claims | Revert to 24-month general; keep fundamental/title separate regime |
| 4 | Limitations/reliance across all claims | Preserve separation of regime categories |
| 5 | General data-room/public-register disclosure | Require specific fair disclosure only |
| 6 | Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion incl. data room | Delete; reintroduce with named knowledge persons |
| 7 | Bluefen reasonable endeavour only | Demand actual consent + condition evidence before Completion |
| 8 | Riverlark post-completion release | Require undertaking + Amelia authority; repay from Completion funds |
| 9 | DD-005 AUD 420k excluded from funds flow | Specific line item or seller-funded |
| 10 | Ironquay AUD 180k closed | Broader indemnity preserved; leave amount open |
| 11 | DD-006 preliminary only | Logs preserved, investigate, update, retain open breach assumption |
| 12 | Sandbar AUD 330k automatic ordinary course | Seller-funded assessment required |
| 13 | Tax / IP closed to general regime | Hold both open |
| 14 | Title via DD-012 only | Independent title/encumbrance evidence required |

**Bottom line:** The Seller's package is below the agreed starting position on nearly every risk-transfer dimension the playbook governs. There is no basis to confirm it as "fair and balanced"; the core terms require mark-up, most substantially the cap reduction, the time limit, the disclosure methodology and the title evidence. Push back on each independently, coordinate the cap, time limit, disclosure and Bluefen positions first, then address the remaining items in sequence.
=== END ADVICE ===
